title: Cost governor with eviction‑resilient model variants and regional soft quotas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a cost governor that enforces soft spend quotas per region and per tenant while preserving latency SLOs through eviction‑resilient model variants. The controller should prefer cheaper spot capacity and lower‑cost GPU classes when safe, fall back to quantized/shorter‑context model variants when preemptions threaten SLOs, and smooth spend across a rolling window to avoid abrupt throttles. Key constraints: maintain 95th percentile latency targets per route, provide transparent billing signals in Console, and avoid customer‑facing errors during spot churn.
acceptance_criteria: Controller enforces per‑region soft quota: when spend reaches 85% of quota, traffic shifts by policy rather than hard reject
95th percentile latency for hedged routes does not exceed baseline +25ms in steady state
Fallback to eviction‑resilient variants reduces on‑demand failover rate by >=40% during simulated spot evictions
Console shows tenant‑level spend smoothing and per‑region quota burn rate with <60s propagation
E2E tests for preemption windows pass in CI; regression suite added to nightly runs
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind tenant opt‑in (opt‑in default false). Start with internal tenants and engineering sandbox accounts.
Phase 1: Canary in us‑west1 with 10 tenants; run 2 weeks of A/B tests measuring latency, cost, and failover rate.
Phase 2: Expand to 25% of production traffic for tenants with lower SLO sensitivity; monitor burn rate and manual kill switch available.
Phase 3: Global gradual rollout with region‑aware defaults; enable opt‑out for high‑priority enterprise tenants.
Rollback: immediate rollback via feature flag; automated failover to current routing algorithm if SLO degradation detected
monitoring_queries: cost_governor.burn_rate_per_tenant_1h: time series showing spend vs quota (per region)
routing.fallback_rate_5m: percent of requests served by fallback model variant
latency.p95_route: 95th percentile latency per route and per tenant
eviction.events_1h: spot eviction events correlated with fallback activations
console.propagation_lag: median time for quota changes to be visible in Console
experiment_plan: Introduce synthetic spot eviction noise in the canary region to validate fallback triggers and hedging behavior.
Run paired A/B experiment: baseline routing vs cost governor with identical traffic; compare cost delta and customer‑visible latency.
Metric thresholds: cost down >=10% for hedged tenants without >10% increase in 95th latency to be considered successful.
Collect qualitative feedback from solutions engineers for enterprise tenants participating in phase 2
notes: Design decision: choose soft quota with weighted degradation vs hard rejects to avoid drop in request success rates
Fallback variants: precompile quantized model (4bit) + reduced context model (+ shorter KV caching) as primary fallback
Cost signals: combine spot availability score with real‑time price delta to decide on immediate vs deferred routing
Smoothing window: use exponential smoothing over 1h with emergency window of 5m for rapid response
